sway: what's the difference between `exec` and `exec_always`, and why doesn't a new `exec` line start on reload?
column2:
exec = run ONCE at session start. exec_always = run at start AND on every `reload`.
`reload` does NOT re-fire `exec` lines, so a newly-added `exec foo` needs logout/in
or a manual run. (exec_always dups the process each reload unless you guard it.)

column1: sway: `$mod+a` seems to lose window focus — what did it do, and how do you get back?
column2:
$mod+a = `focus parent`: climbs the container TREE to the group holding your window
(to retile/move the group as a unit). Descend again with any focus <dir>, or bind
`focus child` ($mod+Shift+a).

column1: sway: an app opens on another workspace and relaunching just focuses it there. Pull it to the current workspace?
column2:
Single-instance apps relaunch to focus, not respawn. Summon via a criteria selector:
  swaymsg '[app_id="org.telegram.desktop"] move workspace current, focus'
Get app_id from: swaymsg -t get_tree

column1: sway: you set `output * bg #062625 solid_color` but the empty workspace is BLACK. Why?
column2:
`bg` is painted by swaybg (optional dep). Not installed ⇒ every background is black,
directive or not. Install swaybg. (Also: two `bg` lines for `*` → the last one wins.)

column1: sway: high-refresh monitor runs at 60 Hz — how do you pin the rate?
column2:
sway takes the output's default mode. List modes with `swaymsg -t get_outputs`, then:
  output HDMI-A-1 mode 1920x1080@200Hz

column1: sway idle: 5-min screen off, 15-min suspend, lock before sleep — swayidle shape?
column2:
exec swayidle -w \
  timeout 300 'swaymsg "output * power off"' resume 'swaymsg "output * power on"' \
  timeout 900 'systemctl suspend' \
  before-sleep 'swaylock -f -c 000000'
-w = finish each cmd first; resume pairs with the timeout ABOVE it. 'power off' is DPMS
(binary, no % dim — a % dim needs brightnessctl/backlight or ddcutil).

column1: Wayland system dark mode with no DE — the one lever, and why Qt apps ignore it?
column2:
gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme 'prefer-dark'  (needs xdg-desktop-portal-gtk).
Broadcasts via the FreeDesktop portal → Firefox/Chrome/Electron/GTK4 follow.
Qt is a SEPARATE track: set QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=kde in ~/.config/environment.d + a dark
KDE scheme (plasma-apply-colorscheme). WPS ignores everything (own skin).

column1: PipeWire: set a default output/input device, and does it persist?
column2:
wpctl status  → note the Sink/Source ID (* = current default).
wpctl set-default <ID>   (reads node type; same cmd for sink or source)
WirePlumber persists the CHOICE per-device across reboots/reconnects (the numeric ID changes).

column1: Bluetooth earbuds: why can't you have good audio AND use their mic at once?
column2:
BT exposes EITHER A2DP (good stereo playback, no mic) OR a headset profile HSP/HFP
(mic, but mono call-quality output) — never both. Switch with:
  pactl set-card-profile bluez_card.XX headset-head-unit   (mic on)
  pactl set-card-profile bluez_card.XX a2dp-sink           (good output back)

column1: waybar: how do you drop a module, and why do clicks on some modules do nothing?
column2:
Remove the module NAME from modules-left/center/right — its config block goes dormant
(no need to delete it). A module reacts to clicks ONLY if given `on-click`; otherwise
it's status text, not a button.

column1: waybar: reload after editing style.css/config without restarting sway?
column2:
killall -SIGUSR2 waybar   # re-reads config + style.css in place.
style.css is GTK3 CSS: @define-color for the palette, .class = live state (#network.disconnected),
box-shadow inset 0 -3px = the underline trick (no layout shift).

column1: A tray applet (arch-update, blueman) launched by sway `exec` never appears in waybar's tray. Fix?
column2:
Race: it docks before waybar's tray module exists. Delay it:
  exec sh -c "sleep 3 && arch-update --tray"

column1: yazi: a `[filetype]` rule using `name` errors. What's the right key, and how do you match all dirs?
column2:
In yazi (26.x) filetype rules key on `url` (path glob) or `mime`, NOT `name` (`name` is
the [icon] section's key). url = "*" → all files, url = "*/" → all directories.
Rules match top-to-bottom, first hit wins → keep the catch-all url="*" LAST.

column1: yazi keymap: shell template placeholders for the hovered file, and how to avoid escaping?
column2:
%h = hovered PATH, %H = hovered URL (file://…), %s/%S = selected paths/URLs.
A trailing `--` disables escaping (everything after is raw). e.g. copy file as uri-list:
  run = '''shell -- printf '%s' "%H" | wl-copy -t text/uri-list'''

column1: yazi: what do `d` and `D` do, and where do trashed files go / how to recover?
column2:
d = move to trash (FreeDesktop → ~/.local/share/Trash/, recoverable).
D = permanently delete (confirmation).
Recover/destroy with trash-cli: trash-list, trash-restore, trash-empty / trash-rm.

column1: tmux: after a sway restart, swaymsg inside tmux fails with 'Unable to connect to …sway-ipc…sock'. Why + fix?
column2:
A long-lived tmux SERVER froze the env at first start; sway's IPC socket path embeds sway's
PID, and a sway restart made a new one → the inherited SWAYSOCK is stale.
Now: tmux kill-server (re-inherits). Durable: set -ga update-environment "SWAYSOCK"
(and WAYLAND_DISPLAY), then detach+reattach.

column1: tmux: `bind -r k select-pane -U` then pressing `h` jumps back to the previous pane. Why, and the fix?
column2:
-r = repeatable: after the bind, tmux stays in a repeat-time window where a BARE hjkl re-fires
without the prefix — so the `h` is read as 'repeat, go left'. Drop -r: use plain
`bind h select-pane -L` … for exactly one move per prefix.
